question: Can the existing state-conditioned object network learn a held-out 100ms collision response, and does supervising all20 future frames impair that same first-frame task?

data.source: existing206train and47reused validation episodes only; no test files
data.event_scope: each pin first contact with ball,another pin,or robot; exclude floor/wall partners; query offset0..150 controls from original prepush anchor; query50..400
data.deduplication: one input window per episode/query; regular and event roles may overlap; each eligible event pin appears once
data.sampling: same rules for training and validation; all windows sampled uniformly with replacement; episode-disjoint splits
data.annotation_boundary: event ticks,pin masks and role flags are selection/scoring metadata only, never model inputs
data.history: 10samples at10Hz plus current; all from times<=query
data.future: 20targets at10Hz; short uses only first target in residual loss; long uses all20

architecture.base: StateProbe(state), ball48/pin81/robot660 encoders480, width256, two8head object attention blocks, independent output times
architecture.control: identical tensors/initialization per seed; short computes exactly the first time slot of the long architecture; no new modules
architecture.inactive_parameters_caveat: short has unused future-only plan projections and output rows; nominal matching is not effective-capacity matching
architecture.state: query rotation matrix9,world linear velocity3,world angular velocity3 per ball/pin; original21points and robot observations/nominal plan retained
architecture.input_statistics: train-only, shared pin statistics, identical between arms

training.loss: equal-present ball/moving-pin/static-pin coordinate MSE; SAME moving mask in both arms, max full2s endpoint displacement>1cm; only supervised time range differs
training.sampler: CPU torch.Generator(seed+1), uniform windows, paired identical index trace
training.early_stopping: none; fixed15000 updates; evaluate every500 including0

evaluation.primary: 100ms endpoint Euclidean error on event pins; average endpoints, then all eligible pin-events within episode, then episodes
evaluation.same_target: short and long BOTH scored on exactly the same first100ms target
evaluation.baselines_scope: comparators only, never added to learned predictions
evaluation.nontrivial_guard: also report event errors where true endpoint displacement>=1mm, plus their count and true response amplitude; no success claim based on near-zero responses
secondary: regular-window never-before-contact pin error and predicted movement>1/2/5mm
evaluation.selection: lowest validation primary over steps0,500,...15000, ties earlier; also compare fixed15000 checkpoints
evaluation.uncertainty: average3seed paired errors within episode before10000paired episode bootstrap draws; seed20261020; reused validation, not a new test

decision.local_learnability: short beats EACH baseline in all3seeds; mean error at least20percent below strongest baseline; paired95CI short-minus-strongest upper<0; same direction at fixed15000 and >=1mm subgroup
decision.horizon_supervision_effect: compare short-long at SAME100ms; evidence requires all3negative deltas, mean>=10percent reduction and paired95CI upper<0; report selected and fixed-step results
decision.interpretation: local success supports studying longer evolution; local failure is recipe/data/representation evidence, not universal impossibility; short-long difference isolates supervision horizon under this recipe, not all architecture choices

scope.compute: one admitted development GPU; sequential runs;6GiB allocator cap

limitations: Privileged current object state is diagnostic, not deployed perception.
Robot interface is unchanged, so this is not complete simulator state.
Both arms change query sampling relative to previous experiments; old and new scores are not an architecture-only comparison.
Supervising one frame changes multi-task gradients and effective active capacity; the comparison does not prove recurrence is necessary.
Reused validation and small numbers of independent collision episodes limit conclusions; bootstrap does not account for all model-selection uncertainty.
